candidates.title: Teaching AI to build scientific models
candidates.summary: 01 A three-step program Teaching AI to build scientific models 01 A three-step program 02 Splitting the bill, or how to constrain models 03 The bill, one level up, or how to build models 04 Lost in translation, or how to interpret models 05 Cells and scales Published Nov 6, 2026 Team Science Topics Discovery Research programs Life sciences See more... AI for Science grantees Jakob Macke , Daniel Gedon , and Stefan Wahl are researchers at the ELLIS Institute Tübingen and the University of Tübingen, where they build AI tools for developing scientific models in neuroscience and beyond. In this guest post, they discuss how AI is starting to change scientific modeling. Related articles Science Nov 4, 2026 Investigating vault particles with Claude View more In 1951, Cambridge University’s computer went out of action for six months. This was inconvenient for physiologist Andrew Huxley, who, alongside his colleague Alan Hodgkin, had just built a set of equations to describe how a particular squid nerve cell fired. The scientists wanted to understand the “action potential” of these nerve cells: the electrical pulses they use to communicate, which underlie everything brains do, from perception to intelligence. The only way to find out whether the equations worked was to solve them and compare the solutions to data. Huxley had hoped to use the newfangled computer to solve the equations.
